articleTitle: Dynamics of process models in PML
publicationTitle: [1989] Proceedings of the 5th International Software Process Workshop
abstract: The Alvey IPSE 2.5 project is concerned with providing support for software developers through executable process models. This position paper outlines the work conducted up to March 1989 to enable interactive definition and enactment of software process models. The work was undertaken by Praxis Systems for STL as part of the IPSE 2.5 project and resulted in: (a) an active process model of an organisation- mini-Praxis; (b) a mechanism whereby active process models can evolve and be customiSed; and (c) the integration and participation of people and existing software tools in the process model.

articleTitle: Acquiring experiences with executable process models
publicationTitle: [1989] Proceedings of the 5th International Software Process Workshop
abstract: The primary thesis of this position paper is that it is mandatory to experiment with executable process models in order to obtain user feedback, to identify requirements on architectural components to support such models, and to investigate the impact of automation in the process itself. This paper briefly describes three generations of investigations with respect to the formalizing, modeling, and encoding of software lifecycle processes. Providing for executable processes has been one of the most important goals of this work.

articleTitle: Conceptual programming
publicationTitle: [1989] Proceedings of the 5th International Software Process Workshop
abstract: The author introduces conceptual programming as a process model based on his programming experiences. Conceptual programming means having programmers work directly with their conceptual models, using their own terms or languages rather than those dictated by the computer. To be useful and effective, conceptual programming must be supported by a powerful programming environment. He has developed such an environment, GARDEN, and is beginning to get feedback on its use.

articleTitle: Describing Working Environments in OPM
publicationTitle: [1989] Proceedings of the 5th International Software Process Workshop
abstract: In OPM, each software process provides a working environment in which programmers can actually work in order to accomplish a designated task, rather than prescribing the algorithm of the task, or giving a behavioral description of the task. We introduce the working environment approach for describing software processes. The key elements of the working environment approach are: (i) the way of using the process programming language to define process templates; (ii) the way of collecting resources and operations in working environments, and (iii) the way of navigating activities performed in working environments.

articleTitle: Session Summary - Mechanisms
publicationTitle: [1989] Proceedings of the 5th International Software Process Workshop
abstract: Takuya Katayama lead the discussion on Mechanisms for Software Process Description. He classified software process views as reflected in the position papers into functional, behavioral and enactional, described some generally desirable properties of software process mechanisms, and listed those projects that seemed to have obtained non-toy experience. He made a plea for each of these projects to answer a questionnaire that, among other things, requested information regarding how the formalism handled ill-behaved processes. The discussion focused on several a variety of issues.
